post.summary: Bulk-mark multiple attendance rows in one round-trip
post.description:
Upserts N attendance rows in a single call. Each row is

(active enrollment, 7-day window, intern exists) are
**best-effort** — failed rows go into `skipped[]` in the
response with a `reason` string instead of failing the
whole batch. Successful rows go into `marked[]`.

Capped at **500 rows per call** as a sanity limit. For
larger imports, paginate the client-side.

The intern-side check-in was removed in Phase 7 — the
admin is the source of truth. Use this endpoint to do an
end-of-week "mark everyone missed today" batch.

Admin override for the daily attendance. Upserts on
`(internId, date)` — a second call with the same date
overwrites the status (and note) instead of creating a
second row. Date must be within the last 7 days, measured
in the **company's timezone**.

For marking N rows at once, prefer
`POST /attendance/bulk-mark` (one round-trip).

Statuses: `attended` | `missed` | `late` | `excused`. The
intern-side check-in was removed — the admin is the source
of truth.

Returns the schedule for `(companyId, programId?)`. When
`programId` is omitted the company default is returned.
The response includes the weekly pattern (`sunday`..
`saturday`), optional `effectiveFrom`/`effectiveTo` date
range, and the program's ObjectId (or null for the default).

If no schedule exists at that scope yet, `schedule` is
`null` and the message is "No schedule configured for this
scope yet".

put.summary: Upsert the attendance schedule (the required-days table)
put.description:
Creates or replaces the schedule for
`(companyId, programId?)`. The `programId` in the body is
optional — omit it to write the company default.

Body: `{ weeklyPattern, programId?, effectiveFrom?,
effectiveTo? }`. `weeklyPattern` must have at least one
day set to `true` (the schema enforces this with a clear
400). `effectiveFrom`/`effectiveTo` are an optional
YYYY-MM-DD range; `effectiveTo: null` means open-ended.

Re-sending the same payload replaces the existing
schedule. There is no DELETE — to clear a schedule
entirely, send an empty `weeklyPattern` would be rejected
(validation), so the admin would have to set every day to
`false` AND drop the schedule row via a one-off script. For
the common case of "swap the schedule", just PUT the new
one.

`evaluations:list:{companyId}:{queryHash}`. Cache is busted
when an evaluation is created / updated / shared at this

(default 20, max 100).

get.summary: Dashboard KPIs + 6-month attendance chart
get.description:
Aggregated view for the company's Evaluations dashboard tab.

**Two parallel aggregations** (one round-trip total):
  1. `companyKpis` — avg attendance (last 30 days), avg
     skill rating + avg overallScore across all evaluations
     ever, count of evaluations created this month.
  2. `monthlyAttendanceChart` — one entry per month for the
     last 6 months, oldest first, with `presentDays`,
     `totalDays`, `rate`.

**Caching:** 60s under `evaluations:dashboard:{companyId}`.
Flushed implicitly on create/update/share via the
`evaluations:{companyId}` prefix flush.

**Known caveat (will fix in Phase 8):** month boundaries
are computed in UTC, so an Egyptian company's "September"
will run Sep 1 00:00 UTC → Sep 30 23:59 UTC instead of
Sep 1 00:00 Cairo → Sep 30 23:59 Cairo. Off by 2 hours at
each edge.

get.summary: At-risk interns (low attendance + overdue reviews)
get.description:
Two lists to surface the red dot on the dashboard:

- `lowAttendance[]` — interns whose 30-day attendance rate
  is below 70% AND who have at least 3 attendance rows in
  the window (so we don't flag someone with one row at
  100% or 0%).
- `evaluationOverdue[]` — interns who have NOT been
  evaluated in the last 30 days (no row, or latest
  `evaluatedAt` is older than 30 days).

**Cap:** 50 interns per call (alerts endpoint, not the full
roster — keep it snappy).

**Caching:** 30s — alerts are time-sensitive.

**Known bug (will fix in Phase 8):** this endpoint still
uses the legacy `enrollmentCompanyId` field to find
interns. After the Phase 5 migration runs, every user who
migrated is missing the legacy field, so this endpoint
returns an empty list. Will switch to `enrollments[].companyId`
+ status filter.

post.summary: Create an evaluation for an intern
post.description:
Admin writes a formal review over a date period. The admin
provides the period + 2 subjective ratings; the service
computes everything else:

  - `attendanceRate` — percent of attendance rows in
    `[period.start, period.end]` with status ∈
    `{attended, late}` (Phase 7 renamed `present` → `attended`,
    `absent` → `missed`; missed and excused both count as
    not-present). Rounded to 2 decimals.
  - `overallScore` — clamped 0..100, weighted
    `0.3*attendanceRate + 0.3*skillPct + 0.2*teamworkPct +
    0.2*engagementScore`. Today `engagementScore = 0` —
    no engagement tracking yet (open follow-up).

**Ratings:** `skillRating` and `teamworkRating` are 0..5.
The service normalizes to the nearest 0.5 (so `4.3 → 4.5`,
`4.7 → 4.5`). Stored values are always in
`{0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, ..., 5}`.

**Scope check:** the intern MUST be actively enrolled at
this company. Returns 400 "This user is not an active
intern at this company" otherwise.

**Fields you type vs the service computes:**
  - you type:  `period`, `skillRating`, `teamworkRating`,
    `strengths?`, `improvements?`, `privateNotes?`
  - service:   `attendanceRate`, `overallScore`,
    `evaluatorId` (from the JWT), `sharedWithIntern: false`

**Notifications:** `EVALUATION_CREATED` is sent to the
intern (so they see a new review in their feed even
before it's shared — they can't read it yet).

**Caching:** invalidates `evaluations:{companyId}` (prefix)
AND `intern:me:{internId}:{companyId}` (per-company view)
+ the legacy single-key `intern:me:{internId}` during the
rollout window. Picker key `intern:enrollments:{internId}`
is NOT flushed (low risk — eval create doesn't mutate
enrollments).

parameters.name: internId
parameters.description: 24-char ObjectId of the intern being reviewed

patch.summary: Update an evaluation (only allowed BEFORE share)
patch.description:
Edit the admin-typed fields on an evaluation. **Refuses
with 400 if `sharedWithIntern: true`** — once the intern
has seen the review, treat it as immutable. There is no
unshare endpoint (open follow-up).

**Re-derives `overallScore` automatically** when the
ratings change. `attendanceRate` is NOT recomputed (the
period is fixed at create time; if attendance changed,
delete this eval and create a new one).

**Mutable fields:** `skillRating`, `teamworkRating`,
`strengths`, `improvements`, `privateNotes`. Period is
NOT mutable — same reason as `attendanceRate`.

**Empty body** is rejected with 400 "At least one field
is required" (Zod refine — no accidental no-ops).

**Caching:** invalidates `evaluations:detail:{evaluationId}`
+ `evaluations:list:{companyId}` (prefix).

**No notification** is sent on update. The intern only
finds out when `sharedWithIntern` flips true.

400.description:
Validation error (bad rating, empty body, ratings out
of range) OR the evaluation has already been shared.

404.description: Evaluation not found at this company

patch.summary: Share an evaluation with the intern
patch.description:
Atomically:
  1. Sets `sharedWithIntern: true`
  2. Stamps `sharedAt = now`
  3. Fires `EVALUATION_SHARED` to the intern

After this call:
  - the evaluation is visible at
    `GET /intern/me/:companyId/evaluations` (with
    `privateNotes` stripped)
  - the admin can no longer PATCH this evaluation
    (returns 400 "Cannot edit an evaluation after it has
    been shared")
  - calling `/share` again is idempotent (returns
    "Evaluation was already shared" — no second notification)

**No body** — the path is the whole request.

**Caching:** invalidates `evaluations:detail:{evaluationId}`
+ `evaluations:list:{companyId}` (prefix). Note: the
intern-side cache key `evaluations:intern:{internId}:
{companyId}` is NOT flushed here, so the intern sees the
update after at most 60s (the per-company TTL). Low risk
(open follow-up).

**Unshare:** not supported today. If you shared by
mistake, contact engineering to flip the flag manually in
Mongo (or wait for the unshare endpoint in a follow-up).

Edit any subset of the mutable fields: `name`, `description`,
`status`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `maxInterns`, `coverImage`.
The body is spread into the update — empty patches are
rejected by Zod refine "at least one field".

**`internIds[]` is NOT mutable** via this endpoint. Use
`POST /:programId/interns` (enroll) or `DELETE
/:programId/interns/:internId` (unenroll) instead.

delete.description:
Marks the program as `status: archived` (soft delete —
reversible by PATCH with `status: active`).

**Soft-cascade:** every project where `programId` points at
this program AND `status != archived` is also archived in
the same call (one `updateMany` on `ProjectModel`).

**Tasks are NOT touched** — the admin can archive those
separately if needed. This was the explicit decision in
the design Q&A: soft-cascade goes Program → Projects, not
Program → Tasks.

**Idempotent:** if the program is already archived, returns
200 with "Program already archived" and skips the cascade.

**Cache flush:** `programs:detail:{programId}` +
`programs:list:{companyId}` + `projects:{companyId}` (prefix
for the cascaded project archive).

post.description:
Adds up to 200 interns to the program's `internIds[]` in one

**Multipart.** Single `file` field. The old attachment (if

**Atomic swap:** the new file is uploaded FIRST, then the DB
is updated. If the DB update fails, the new Cloudinary file
is destroyed (best-effort) so we don't leak storage. The
OLD file is only destroyed after the DB update succeeds — so
we never lose the old attachment on a failure.

`DELETE /attachment` endpoint today (open follow-up). For
now, upload an empty placeholder via PUT.

`image/jpg`, `application/pdf`. Per-file size cap: 2 MB at

- `target: "program"` — fan out to every intern in

- `target: "project"` — fan out to every intern in

- `target: "intern"`  — single recipient; `internId` required.

For broadcast targets (company / program / project), one
task row is created per active member and they all share
the same `taskGroupId` in the response. If the target has
zero active members, the endpoint returns **400**.

Each intern gets one `TASK_ASSIGNED` notification. The
response shape differs by target:

- `target: "intern"` → `{ task }` (one row)
- broadcast          → `{ tasks, count, groupId, target, members }`

post.summary: Move a task through the kanban state machine
post.description:
Enforces the state machine from `src/utils/taskStateMachine.ts`.
Two actor roles share the machine; this endpoint always acts
as admin (full set of transitions).

**Admin transitions allowed:**
- `todo`        → `in_progress`, `complete`
- `in_progress` → `in_review`, `complete`
- `in_review`   → `in_progress` (send back), `complete`
- `complete`    → terminal (no outgoing)
- `archived`    → terminal (no outgoing — use `/transition` to
  move an active task back; archiving is the DELETE endpoint)

**Side effects:**
- `→ complete`: stamps `reviewedAt = now`, accepts optional
  `reviewerFeedback` and `pointsAwarded`, fires
  `TASK_REVIEWED` with `approved: true` to the intern.
- `in_review → in_progress` (admin send-back): clears
  `submittedAt` so the next submit is a fresh one, fires
  `TASK_REVIEWED` with `approved: false`.

**400 "Cannot transition from X to Y"** if the move isn't
allowed. **400 "Cannot transition an archived task"** if
the source row is archived.

get.summary: My evaluations at this company (only sharedWithIntern)
get.description:
Returns the authenticated intern's evaluations that have
been shared with them AND belong to the company in the path.

intern cannot read another intern's reviews.

**Three-layer scope check** (defense in depth):
  1. `requireIntern()` — role gate (or any active enrollment)
  2. `hasActiveEnrollmentAt(user, companyId)` — intern must
     be active AT THIS company (404 otherwise)
  3. Query filter is hard-coded to
     `internId = res.locals.user._id` AND
     `companyId = path :companyId` AND
     `sharedWithIntern = true` — the intern literally
     cannot pass these as query params; they're enforced
     server-side.

**Filter:**
  - `period` — `YYYY` or `YYYY-MM`, regex-matched on
    `period.start` (so `period=2026` matches every
    evaluation starting in 2026).

**Projection:** the service strips `privateNotes` before
returning rows. The intern sees everything else, including
`attendanceRate`, `skillRating`, `teamworkRating`,
`overallScore`, the strengths/improvements text, and the
`sharedAt` timestamp.

**Sort:** most recently shared first (`sharedAt: -1`),
so a freshly-released review shows up at the top.

**Pagination:** `page` (1-based, default 1) + `limit`
(default 20, max 100).

**Caching:** 60s under
`evaluations:intern:{internId}:{companyId}:{queryHash}`.
**Not** flushed when the admin shares an evaluation — the
intern sees the update after at most 60s (open follow-up).

post.summary: Add a course, optionally with a certificate, in one call
post.description:
Unified endpoint to add a course to the authenticated user's profile.
The `file` field is optional — if omitted, the course is created with
no certificate and you can attach one later via
`/user/upload/course-certificate/{courseIndex}`. If the certificate
upload fails, the course is NOT created (atomic — no orphan course
pointing at a missing file).

Optional date-window and description fields are accepted as
multipart text fields. `present: true` means "still in progress"
and `endDate` is ignored in that case.

endDate.description: When the course ended. Ignored when `present=true`.

present.description: True if the course is still ongoing.

file.description: Optional certificate (image or PDF, max 2 MB).

201.description: Course added successfully (with or without certificate)

index.description: Index of the new course in the user's `courses` array

certificateUrl.description: Authenticated file-proxy URL (PDF certificates only); fetch it with the bearer token to open the PDF inline in the browser, same as the CV/resume.

400.description: Missing/invalid name or unsupported file type

patch.summary: Update one of the user's courses (rename, edit dates, description, and/or replace certificate)
patch.description:
Updates the course at `courseIndex` in the authenticated user's
`courses` array. Every field is optional — send only what changes.
Replacing the certificate uploads the new asset first and destroys
the old Cloudinary file afterwards, so a failed upload leaves the
course untouched. Returns 404 when no course exists at that index.

`present: true` means "still in progress" and `endDate` is
ignored. To clear `endDate`, send the empty string.

endDate.description: New end date. Ignored when `present=true`. Pass empty string to clear.

present.description: True if the course is still ongoing.

file.description: Replacement certificate — image or PDF, max 2 MB (optional)

certificateUrl.description: Authenticated file-proxy URL (PDF certificates only); fetch it with the bearer token to open the PDF inline, same as the CV/resume.

400.description: Invalid course index / invalid name / nothing to update / invalid date window / unsupported file type

delete.summary: Delete one of the user's courses
delete.description:
Removes the course at `courseIndex` from the authenticated user's
`courses` array. The associated Cloudinary certificate (if any)
is destroyed after the DB delete succeeds, so a failed delete
never leaves the user's profile pointing at a missing asset.
Returns 404 when no course exists at that index.

removedCount.description: Number of courses removed (1 on success, 0 when not found).

403.description: You can only view your own applications

get.summary: Proxy a Cloudinary file with correct Content-Type
get.description:
Serves a raw Cloudinary asset (PDF, doc, image) with the right
Content-Type header so browsers can open it inline. Requires a
valid bearer token, the `url` query param must point to a
resource in the configured Cloudinary cloud, redirects are
refused, and the response is capped at 10 MB.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Filename with extension (e.g. `resume.pdf`). The extension determines the Content-Type.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Fully-encoded Cloudinary URL of the file to fetch.

200.description: File body streamed with the correct Content-Type.

400.description: Missing/invalid `url` or `url` does not target the configured Cloudinary cloud.

get.summary: Liveness probe
get.description:
Public health check. Use this for uptime monitoring and load-balancer
probes. Returns the process uptime in seconds and the current
status of the Redis cache (when one is configured).
